LESSON: LETTER SOUNDS AND LETTER NAMES-PHONICS

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: WRITING
Topic 4.1: Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write upper and lower case 3 lessons
2. differentiate letters with visual similarities (bdp) (w, vym) (k)
3. sound digraphs and consonant clusters
4. develop an interest in writing using uppercase and letter names correctly e) handwrite letters, numbers, and symbols sound confusion (b, p) (d, t) (m, n)] 140 Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: Learners play games that help in developing fine motor skills in pairs and groups.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. write upper and lower case 3 lessons
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to write upper and lower case 3 lessons. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. differentiate letters with visual similarities (bdp) (w, vym) (k)
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to differentiate letters with visual similarities (bdp) (w, vym) (k). Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. sound digraphs and consonant clusters
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to sound digraphs and consonant clusters. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. develop an interest in writing using uppercase and letter names correctly e) handwrite letters, numbers, and symbols sound confusion (b, p) (d, t) (m, n)] 140 Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: Learners play games that help in developing fine motor skills in pairs and groups.

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics.
2. Explain Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics.
4. Show that you can: write upper and lower case 3 lessons
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Letter Sounds and letter names-Phonics important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. write upper and lower case 3 lessons
2. differentiate letters with visual similarities (bdp) (w, vym) (k)
3. sound digraphs and consonant clusters
4. develop an interest in writing using uppercase and letter names correctly e) handwrite letters, numbers, and symbols sound confusion (b, p) (d, t) (m, n)] 140 Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: Learners play games that help in developing fine motor skills in pairs and groups.
